gloss: scorched rice crust; crispy rice at the bottom of the pot

definitions.gloss: scorched rice crust; crispy rice at the bottom of the pot
definitions.explanation: The thin, crispy layer of rice that forms at the bottom of a pot or rice cooker when rice is cooked over direct heat. Considered a delicacy in many cuisines.

examples.japanese: お{焦|こ}げが{好|す}きです。
examples.english: I like the crispy rice crust.

examples.japanese: {土鍋|どなべ}で{炊|た}くと{美味|おい}しいお{焦|こ}げができる。
examples.english: When you cook rice in a clay pot, you get delicious scorched rice.

examples.japanese: お{焦|こ}げにお{茶|ちゃ}をかけて{食|た}べるのが{祖母|そぼ}の{楽|たの}しみだった。
examples.english: Pouring tea over the scorched rice and eating it was my grandmother's little pleasure.

notes:
The お is an honorific/beautifying prefix attached to {焦|こ}げ (burnt part), from the verb {焦|こ}げる (to scorch, to burn). Also written as おこげ in hiragana. The kanji form {御焦|おこ}げ is rarely used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{焦|こ}げができる (for scorched rice to form)
- お{焦|こ}げにお{湯|ゆ}をかける (to pour hot water over scorched rice)
- {土鍋|どなべ}のお{焦|こ}げ (clay pot scorched rice)
- パリパリのお{焦|こ}げ (crispy scorched rice)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {焦|こ}げ — burnt part, scorch; the general term without the honorific prefix, can refer to any burnt food
- {焦|こ}げ{目|め} — browned surface, grill marks; the intentional browning on food
- {煎餅|せんべい} — rice cracker; a separate snack made from rice

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional Japanese cooking with {釜|かま} (iron pots) or {土鍋|どなべ} (clay pots), お{焦|こ}げ was a natural byproduct. Many people consider it a treat. A classic way to enjoy it is お{焦|こ}げ{湯|ゆ} — pouring hot water or tea over the crispy rice to make a simple, comforting drink-food.
